newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates dip on surplus stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates dip on surplus stocks.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates dipped on Tuesday as ginners tried to unload surplus stocks before the arrival of 1997/98 (July-June) crop in July, dealers said.

"There is panic among ginners because they have large quantitities of unsold cotton stocks from the 1996/97 crop," said dealer Adil Usman. "Selling pressure has brought the prices down as most deals are being made on credit."
Pakistan's cotton output has reached 8.73 million bales in 1996/97 and there are 1.508 million bales of unsold stocks available," the Cotton Export Corporation of Pakistan said.
